items.title: AWS Billing and Cost Management now supports AWS Billing Conductor and AWS Billing Transfer views as source views for custom billing views
items.summary:
Custom billing views now support AWS Billing Conductor and AWS Billing Transfer views as source views. These are the views AWS maintains per billing group and per billing transfer relationship. You can combine them into a single custom billing view, apply filters, and use that view in Cost Explorer, AWS Budgets, and the Billing and Cost Management console. There are three source view types. Billing group views contain the cost of each Billing Conductor billing group, which you can combine for chargeback and showback across business units. Billing transfer views contain the cost transferred to you for each end customer, and transfer showback views contain the cost that end customer sees. Aggregating each type gives you your total transferred cost and the total bill your end customers see.

Your access does not change: you can use an AWS-managed view as a source only where you can already access it. Once created, you can share a custom billing view using AWS Resource Access Manager with accounts inside or outside your organization, so your finance team or a downstream seller works with the data in their own account. Whether you are an AWS Partner reselling AWS services or an organization using billing groups for pro forma billing, you get one consolidated view instead of one per customer or group.

This feature is available in all commercial AWS Regions at no additional cost. To get started, navigate to Billing Views in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console or view the user guide.

items.title: Amazon EC2 G7 instances now available in additional regions
items.summary:
Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) G7 instances powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs are now available in Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Mumbai, Sydney) and South America (Sao Paulo) Regions. G7 instances deliver up to 4.6x AI inference performance and up to 2.1 graphics performance compared to G6 instances. G7 instances also deliver faster performance for GPU-accelerated data analytics workloads.

Customers can use G7 instances for deploying AI models for language translation, video and image analysis, speech recognition and recommender systems. They also accelerate graphics workloads such as creating and rendering real-time, cinematic-quality graphics and game streaming. Additionally, G7 instances support video transcoding, spatial computing, and data analytics workloads. G7 instances feature up to 8 NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs with 32 GB of memory per GPU and custom Intel Xeon 6 processors. They support up to 192 virtual CPUs (vCPUs) and up to 700 Gbps of Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) networking bandwidth. They also support up to 768 GiB of system memory, and up to 7.6 TB of local NVMe SSD storage.

You can use G7 instances for Amazon EC2 in the following AWS Regions: US West (Oregon), US East (N. Virginia, Ohio) , Europe (London, Spain, Frankfurt, Stockholm) , Asia Pacific (Mumbai, Sydney) and South America (Sao Paulo). You can purchase G7 instances as On-Demand Instances, Spot Instances, or as part of Savings Plans.

To get started, visit the AWS Management Console, AWS Command Line Interface (CLI), and AWS SDKs. To learn more, visit the G7 instance page.

items.title: Amazon OpenSearch Service announces managed cross-Region disaster recovery
items.summary:
Amazon OpenSearch Service now offers managed cross-Region disaster recovery, so you can meet strict availability and business continuity requirements for mission-critical search, AI, and analytics workloads without building or maintaining replication yourself. After you create domains in two Regions, you can pair them with a single API call or a few steps in the AWS Management Console.

Managed disaster recovery delivers a recovery point objective (RPO) of under one minute and a recovery time objective (RTO) of under 20 minutes. The secondary domain stays continuously in sync with the primary. For planned events such as maintenance or Region rotation, a switchover swaps the two domains' roles with zero data loss. If your primary domain becomes unavailable, a failover promotes the secondary, with data loss limited to the replication lag. After a failover, you restore protection by pairing the new primary with a secondary domain. You can monitor replication health and lag with Amazon CloudWatch metrics.

Managed disaster recovery requires OpenSearch 3.7 or later and supports domains in the same AWS account, including domains encrypted with customer managed AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys. Domains that use UltraWarm storage or OpenSearch Optimized instances (OR1 or OR2) aren't supported. If you're on an earlier version, clone-based upgrades let you test OpenSearch 3.7 against your workload, cut over when you're ready, and roll back if needed.

There's no additional charge for managed disaster recovery. You pay standard rates for the secondary domain and cross-Region data transfer. For details, see Amazon OpenSearch Service pricing.

Managed disaster recovery is available today in all commercial AWS Regions where Amazon OpenSearch Service is available (Region list). To get started, see the disaster recovery documentation.

items.title: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL announces Extended Support minor versions 13.23-rds.20260819, 12.22-rds.20260820 and 11.22-rds.20260822
items.summary:
Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS) for PostgreSQL announces Amazon RDS Extended Support minor versions 13.23-rds.20260819, 12.22-rds.20260820 and 11.22-rds.20260822.

Amazon RDS Extended Support provides up to three additional years of fixes for critical Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) and bugs beyond a major version's end of standard support date, giving you more time to upgrade to a new major version.

You can upgrade your database using Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments, in-place upgrade, or restore from a snapshot. Learn more about performing version upgrades in the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL User Guide.

Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL makes it simple to set up, operate, and scale PostgreSQL deployments in the cloud. Create or update a fully managed Amazon RDS database in the Amazon RDS Management Console or by using the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI).

items.title: Amazon RDS for MySQL 26.10 is now available in Amazon RDS Database Preview Environment
items.summary:
Starting today, Amazon RDS for MySQL 26.10 is available in the Amazon RDS Database Preview Environment, allowing you to evaluate the pre-release of MySQL 26.10 on Amazon RDS for MySQL.

MySQL 26.10 includes bug fixes, security patches, and some improvements to READ COMMITTED workload performance and purge lag warnings in the error log. On busy READ COMMITTED workloads, NUMA systems performance could be impacted as each read view that closed required a global mutex. Read-view objects can now be reused which eliminates the global mutex on closure. The error log now reports warnings when the history-list length (HLL) crosses innodb_max_purge_lag and when purge lag begins delaying DML, so you can detect purge backlogs before they affect performance. To learn more, please refer to the MySQL 26.10 release notes.

Amazon RDS Database Preview Environment database instances are retained for a maximum period of 60 days and are automatically deleted after the retention period. Amazon RDS database snapshots that are created in the Preview Environment can only be used to create or restore database instances within the Preview Environment. Amazon RDS Database Preview Environment database instances are priced as per the pricing in the US East (Ohio) Region.

items.title: AWS Partner Central now provides an improved business planning experience
items.summary:
AWS Partner Central now offers a new business planning experience in the AWS Console. AWS Partners can initiate plans for growing their AWS business or collaborate on plans initiated by AWS teams.

Partners can collaborate with AWS partner development, technology, marketing, and specialist teams to define plan narratives, goals, and initiatives. AI-assisted plan readiness scores help partners identify areas to improve, while real-time tracking shows progress against goals. Partners can also add attachments and export plans to prepare for business reviews.

Partners can use application programming interfaces (APIs) and software development kits (SDKs) to integrate business planning into their workflows. Programmatic notifications are also available.

Business planning is available to AWS Partners who are actively engaged with AWS Partner management teams. AWS Partner Central is available in the US East (N. Virginia) Region. To get started, sign in to AWS Partner Central and choose Business Plan.

items.title: Amazon S3 Access Grants now support listing grants across multiple AWS accounts
items.summary:
Amazon S3 Access Grants can now discover and list all your grants across multiple AWS accounts with a single API call, eliminating the need to query each account separately. A single ListCallerAccessGrants call returns grants from your own S3 Access Grants instance and every instance shared with you, giving you a complete view of the S3 data you can access.

By setting the new InstanceScope parameter to ALL in your ListCallerAccessGrants request, S3 Access Grants queries every instance shared with you through AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) and returns all the grants in one combined response, each identifying the account that owns it. Additionally, when you request credentials with GetDataAccess for an S3 path and set InstanceScope to ALL, S3 Access Grants locates the owning account for you, routes the request to its instance, and returns credentials for the matching grant.

This capability is now available in all AWS Regions where S3 Access Grants is available, at no additional cost. You can use the AWS SDK, API, or CLI to list and access grants across accounts. To learn more, visit the S3 Access Grants overview page and the S3 documentation.

items.title: Amazon Bedrock adds bedrock-runtime endpoint support for Daybreak models
items.summary:
Eligible customers can now access OpenAI’s specialized cybersecurity models Daybreak Red: GPT-5.6 Cyber and Daybreak Blue: GPT-5.6 Sol through the bedrock-runtime endpoint on Amazon Bedrock.

Daybreak Blue is the starting point for most security teams across defensive workflows, including vulnerability discovery, detection engineering, and incident response. Daybreak Red is designed for advanced, authorized tasks such as vulnerability research, exploit reproduction, and mitigation development. For these tasks, a lower refusal threshold, matched by stronger identity verification, monitoring, and access controls, improves the speed and depth of an investigation. Your inference data is not used for model training, and neither model requires you to opt in to sharing your data with OpenAI.

On the bedrock-runtime endpoint, the models are available through US and Global cross-Region inference (CRIS) profiles. Access to the models requires enrollment in Daybreak access from OpenAI. To enroll, contact OpenAI or reach out to your AWS account team for guidance on eligibility. Once approved, work with your account team to request access on AWS. For regional availability through the bedrock-mantle endpoint and more information, view the documentation.

items.title: Amazon S3 Tables now support S3 server access logging
items.summary:
Amazon S3 Tables now support server access logging, providing you detailed records of the requests made to your table buckets. You can now track table operations, namespace management, and data access to support security audits, access analysis, and cost attribution. Log delivery is available at no additional cost, and you pay only for the storage of the log files.

When you enable server access logging on a table bucket, S3 delivers logs for requests to all tables and namespaces in that bucket to a general purpose bucket in the same account and Region. Each record captures the requester, operation, table name, namespace, response status, and request timing, using the same space-delimited format as S3 server access logs for general purpose buckets. This lets you reuse your existing log analysis workflows to query S3 Table logs with any query engine of your choice such as Amazon Athena and DuckDB.

Server access logging for S3 Tables is available in all AWS Regions where S3 Tables are available. You can enable it using the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, or AWS CloudFormation. To learn more, visit the S3 Tables overview page and S3 Tables server access logging in the Amazon S3 User Guide.

items.title: AWS Marketplace SaaS free trials now convert automatically to paid subscriptions
items.summary:
Today, AWS Marketplace announces that free trials of usage-based software as a service (SaaS) products can now convert automatically to paid subscriptions. When a free trial ends, the buyer's subscription continues at the seller's usage-based pricing, so buyers pay only for what they use after the trial. This helps sellers turn more trial users into paying customers. Buyers get a simple way to evaluate software before they buy, with no new subscription and no interruption in access.

Sellers can offer a free trial of 7 to 90 days that converts to a paid subscription at the price they set. For example, a data team can try an analytics product for 30 days and, if it meets their needs, keep using it after the trial ends. Buyers see the trial length, conversion date, and pricing before they subscribe. They receive reminder emails before the trial converts and can cancel at any time before conversion at no charge.

Sellers can create a free trial in AWS Partner Central, or update an existing free trial offer to convert automatically. This capability is available for public offers in all AWS Regions where AWS Marketplace is available.

To learn more, see the AWS Marketplace Seller Guide and the AWS Marketplace Buyer Guide.

items.title: AWS Network Firewall launches next-generation firewall policy
items.summary:
Today, AWS announces next-generation firewall (NGFW) policy for AWS Network Firewall, a new policy model that provides security teams with a simpler policy structure and increased rule capacity. AWS Network Firewall is a managed network security service that protects your Amazon VPCs with access control and threat detection.

The new policy model strengthens your security posture by layering firewall and IPS protections instead of combining them, which also makes policies easier to manage. You author firewall rules that enforce deny-by-default access control, such as allowing traffic only to approved domains. For IPS rules, you can use managed rule groups from AWS or AWS Marketplace partners, which update automatically as new threats emerge. You can also create your own custom IPS rule groups. Firewall and IPS rules each have their own capacity, so you no longer trade one off against the other. For rules you don't share across policies, you can create embedded rule groups that draw capacity on demand without pre-allocation. With NGFW policy, all rules are stateful and evaluate with full connection context, for consistent, predictable traffic handling. Your existing policies continue to operate without changes, and IPS rules remain backward compatible.

NGFW policy is available at no additional charge in all commercial AWS Regions and AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. For a full list of supported regions, visit the AWS Capabilities by Region page.

To learn more, see the AWS Network Firewall product page and documentation.

items.title: Amazon ElastiCache Serverless now supports vector, full-text and hybrid searches plus aggregations
items.summary:
Amazon ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey now supports vector, full-text, and hybrid search, along with aggregations. Applications searching live data often face a hard trade-off between latency and recall, along with delays before updates become searchable. With search on ElastiCache Serverless, applications can search data with latency as low as microseconds at up to 99% recall for vector search, while serving billions of queries per day. Updates are searchable in as little as microseconds, as soon as writes complete.

Search on ElastiCache Serverless is ideal for latency-sensitive applications with unpredictable traffic and for teams that want to get started with search quickly. You can combine search types in a single query, tune recall as needed, and analyze results with server-side aggregations. Developers can give every agent, session, or task its own datastore for memory and context retrieval, so agents can experiment, fail, and retry without touching production or each other. Each datastore is ready in seconds, reachable over a public endpoint with no network setup, and billed only for what it uses, with zero infrastructure to manage. Applications can also power product discovery, recommendation systems, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).

Search is available on ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey in all commercial AWS Regions, AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, and the AWS European Sovereign Cloud Region on ElastiCache version 9 for Valkey. Valkey is the most permissive open source and vendor-neutral alternative to Redis and the recommended engine for ElastiCache. To get started, create a new serverless cache or upgrade an existing one to Valkey 9 using the AWS Management Console, AWS SDK, or AWS CLI. To learn more, see the ElastiCache documentation. For pricing, see the ElastiCache pricing page.

items.title: Amazon GameLift Servers now supports Game Session Placement Insights
items.summary:
Amazon GameLift Servers now offers Game Session Placement Insights, delivering detailed, per-placement diagnostic logs for game session queue routing. Amazon GameLift Servers routes game session placement requests through queues that evaluate multiple fleet locations based on latency and cost factors. This feature is designed for game developers and engineers who need greater transparency into how their game session queues operate.

Previously, developers had limited visibility into why placements succeeded, failed, or timed out, making queue optimization difficult. Game Session Placement Insights captures which fleet locations were evaluated, the player latency and cost factors that influenced routing decisions, and the final placement outcome for every placement. This enables teams to identify patterns such as consistently slow placements, repeated failures, or sessions landing in unexpected locations, and to tune their queues to improve the overall player experience.

You can enable this feature per queue and deliver logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, Amazon S3, and Amazon Data Firehose. Game Session Placement Insights is available in all supported Amazon GameLift Servers regions.

To learn more about Game Session Placement Insights and how to get started, visit the Amazon GameLift Servers documentation.

items.title: CloudWatch PromQL alarms now support EC2 and Application Auto Scaling
items.summary:
Amazon CloudWatch alarms that use Prometheus Query Language (PromQL) can now trigger Amazon EC2 and Application Auto Scaling step and simple scaling policies. You can scale your EC2 Auto Scaling groups on CloudWatch OpenTelemetry metrics using the same kind of PromQL queries you use for dashboards and alerting.

In this release, PromQL alarms also support EC2 Auto Scaling simple and step scaling policies. Target tracking is not currently a supported policy type for PromQL alarms. Teams moving to OpenTelemetry can scale capacity on the same metrics as the rest of their monitoring, instead of keeping separate classic metric alarms for scaling. For step scaling, how far the value is past the threshold in your PromQL query decides which step applies. The query must return a single series and compare it to a threshold.

You can add EC2 Auto Scaling and Application Auto Scaling actions in the CloudWatch console when you create or edit an alarm, or with the PutMetricAlarm API, AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, or AWS CloudFormation. You can also use the PutMetricAlarm API, AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, or AWS CloudFormation.

This feature is available in all AWS Regions where CloudWatch PromQL alarms are available. Standard CloudWatch alarm pricing applies. To get started, see  Using PromQL in alarms  and  Alarm actions  in the Amazon CloudWatch User Guide.

items.title: Amazon OpenSearch Service now lets you validate and roll back version upgrades
items.summary:
Amazon OpenSearch Service now supports clone-based upgrades, which let you validate a new OpenSearch version alongside your current one and cut over to it only when you're satisfied. If you find a problem, you can cancel before you cut over or roll back afterward. With clone-based upgrades, you can move to new versions with more confidence.

When you start a clone-based upgrade, OpenSearch Service copies the data from your existing cluster (the primary cluster) to a second cluster running the new version (the cloned cluster). While the primary cluster keeps serving your workload, you can run the same search queries on both clusters and compare their performance using Amazon CloudWatch metrics. After you finish validating, you can cut over to the cloned cluster. If you keep the previous version for a retention period you choose, you can roll back to it at any time during that period. You can start and manage a clone-based upgrade from the AWS Management Console, the AWS CLI, or the OpenSearch Service APIs.

Clone-based upgrades are available for domains running OpenSearch 1.1 or later, or Elasticsearch 7.10, in AWS Commercial Regions where Amazon OpenSearch Service is offered, except Asia Pacific (New Zealand), Asia Pacific (Taipei), Asia Pacific (Thailand), and Mexico (Central). For a complete list of Regions, see the AWS Region Table.

To learn more, see Upgrading Amazon OpenSearch Service domains in the Amazon OpenSearch Service Developer Guide. To get started, visit the Amazon OpenSearch Service product page.

items.title: Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) now supports post-quantum TLS, wildcard indexes, and $unionWith in version 8.0.3
items.summary:
Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) 8.0.3 adds hybrid post-quantum key exchange for TLS, wildcard indexes, the $unionWith aggregation stage, and new change stream events. Post-quantum TLS protects data in transit from traffic that is recorded today and decrypted later with a quantum computer. The new MongoDB APIs let you move more MongoDB workloads to Amazon DocumentDB without changing application code.

What's new in 8.0.3:

  • Post-quantum TLS: TLS 1.3 connections use hybrid key exchange based on the Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism (ML-KEM) when the client supports it. Other clients keep using classical key exchange. Two new Amazon CloudWatch metrics, TLSHandshakesClassical and TLSHandshakesPostQuantum, count the handshakes of each type.

  • Wildcard indexes: index every field, or every field under a path, to query documents with dynamic schemas.

  • Aggregation: $unionWith combines results from multiple collections in one pipeline. $lookup and $graphLookup work in views, and correlated $lookup sub-pipelines accept $unionWith and $facet.

  • Change streams: dropIndex() and dropIndexes() now emit dropIndexes events.

  • Compression metrics: collStats and stats() report per-collection input bytes, output bytes, and compression ratio.

Amazon DocumentDB 8.0.3 is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon DocumentDB is offered. To learn more, see the Amazon DocumentDB Developer Guide.

items.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore now offers a Web Search API
items.summary:
Today, AWS announces the general availability of the Web Search API on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, which lets you search the web with a single API call. Web Search on AgentCore has been available as an MCP tool through AgentCore Gateway. The new InvokeWebSearch API gives applications, custom agent loops, and data pipelines search results with no resources to create.

The API returns ranked results from the Amazon-operated web index behind Web Search on AgentCore. Each result includes a text extract and, when available, the page title, URL, and publication time. You can filter each request by domain and publication time, for example to find recent product announcements or check a claim against trusted domains.

You call the API with the AWS SDKs or the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) and authorize calls with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). You can call it from your virtual private cloud (VPC) through AWS PrivateLink and log requests as AWS CloudTrail data events. Web Search API queries are billed at $7 per 1,000 queries, the same rate as Web Search through AgentCore Gateway, with no gateway charges.

The Web Search API is available in US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Europe (Ireland). To learn more, see Search the web with the InvokeWebSearch API in the AgentCore Developer Guide, the Web Search  page, and AgentCore pricing .

items.title: Amazon CloudWatch Logs announces account-level retention policies
items.summary:
Amazon CloudWatch Logs now supports account-level retention policies, so you can use a single policy to set how long log data is kept across all or subset of log groups in an AWS account. Account-level policies allow platform and security teams to bring each log group in line with their retention standards.

With today's launch, you can create policies that cover all log groups in the account or apply to a specific set of log groups with names that start with a prefix, such as /aws/lambda. You can additionally choose whether it applies to existing log groups or only new ones. When more than one policy matches a log group, the longest retention period applies. For example, a central platform team can set a 90-day baseline for the account and a 1-year policy for log groups that start with /security to meet audit requirements, without tracking individual log group names.

Account-level retention policies are available in all commercial AWS Regions except Middle East (Bahrain), and Middle East (UAE) at no additional cost . You can create and manage up to 20 policies per account and region using the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, and AWS SDKs. Learn more in the  CloudWatch Logs documentation, and the  API reference .

items.title: AWS Glue adds 100 new native connectors for popular SaaS applications
items.summary:
AWS Glue now supports 100 new native connectors that simplify access to data in popular SaaS and REST API-based applications. Previously, bringing data from SaaS applications into AWS required writing custom code. Now, teams can create a connection once in the AWS Glue Data Catalog and reuse it across ETL jobs with the same permissions model they already use for AWS Glue.

The new connectors span generative AI, finance, payments, marketing, product analytics, human resources, engineering, IT operations, and collaboration tools. AI teams can bring usage and cost data from model providers such as Anthropic to track generative AI adoption and spend. Finance teams can consolidate transactions from applications such as Adyen, Square, and Xero for faster reporting. Product and marketing teams can combine billing, usage, and campaign data from tools such as Chargebee, Amplitude, and Klaviyo to understand customer lifetime value. HR teams can unify workforce data from systems such as BambooHR and Gusto for headcount planning. Engineering teams can join incident and deployment data from tools such as PagerDuty, Sentry, Jenkins, and Vercel to track reliability. You can load the integrated data into Amazon S3 or Amazon Redshift for analytics and reporting.

The 100 new AWS Glue connectors are available in all AWS Commercial Regions on Glue versions 5.0 and above.

To learn more, see the complete list of available connectors and learn about connecting to individual connectors in the AWS Glue documentation.

items.title: AWS STS now supports cross-partition federation for AWS identities
items.summary:
AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) now lets your workloads use their AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) identity in one partition to get temporary credentials for an IAM role in a different partition, without storing long-term credentials, which can help improve your security posture. Partitions are groups of AWS Regions, such as the commercial and AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, and each partition has an independent instance of IAM, creating a hard boundary between them. Previously, organizations that run workloads across partitions commonly relied on long-term credentials, such as IAM user access keys, that don't expire automatically.

With this launch, your workload requests a short-lived token from AWS STS in its own partition and exchanges it for temporary AWS credentials in the other partition, using the existing GetWebIdentityToken and AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity APIs. You control which identities can access each role, apply governance across your organization, and audit token use in AWS CloudTrail in both partitions. This launch helps with scenarios such as consolidated security and compliance reporting, and centralized operations tooling. If your organization already operates a public key infrastructure (PKI), IAM Roles Anywhere is another option for cross-partition access.

Cross-partition federation is available at no additional charge in all commercial AWS Regions, the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, the China Regions, and the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Region. To learn more, see Federating AWS identities across AWS partitions in the IAM User Guide and the blog post Simplify cross-partition access with AWS IAM outbound identity federation.

items.title: Amazon Quick is now AWS Quick
items.summary:
Amazon Quick, the AI workspace built only for work, is now AWS Quick, a name that reflects the enterprise security and governance built into Quick from the start as an AWS service. The new name now appears across the Quick website, the web, desktop, and mobile apps, and AWS documentation. Existing customers don't need to take any action, and Quick works the same way it did before.

Amazon Quick Sight, the business intelligence capability in Quick, is now AWS Quick Sight. Quick Sight customers can keep using their dashboards, datasets, and analyses just as they do today, with no changes to their data, settings, or pricing.

With Quick, teams use AI agents to research, analyze, and act across the data and applications they already use, regardless of vendor. Quick understands your role, your team, and how your work connects, and anyone can build agents, apps, and automations in plain language that become shared assets for the whole team. Quick is HIPAA eligible and holds compliance certifications including FedRAMP, SOC 2, and ISO 27001. Your data stays in your environment and never trains someone else's models.

AWS Quick is available in many AWS Regions. For more information, see the AWS Region table.

To learn more, see AWS Quick.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 is now available on AWS GovCloud (US)
items.summary:
Claude Fable 5.2 is now available on AWS GovCloud (US) and brings Anthropic's most capable generally available model for technical work to regulated customers. Fable 5.2 sets a new standard on the hardest projects in coding, math, and science, and Anthropic recommends it for fields like software engineering, scientific research, and finance, where judgment, iteration, and accuracy are critical. Claude Mythos 5.2, the same underlying model as Claude Fable 5.2, with its full cyber and bio capabilities retained for cybersecurity and biology research, is available through Anthropic’s verification programs.

Claude Fable 5.2 can work for hours and up to days unattended, driving autonomous work and taking on bigger, more challenging projects. It takes on large, loosely defined engineering problems across multiple repositories and monorepos, tests its own work as it goes, and is more willing to question inherited conclusions, so it finds root causes previous Claude models miss. In Anthropic’s testing, it coordinated hundreds of subagents as a lead agent and flagged results that don't reproduce. Beyond coding, it develops new analytical methods for scientific research and brings frontier reasoning to quantitative finance.

Anthropic has designated Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 as covered models, which require data retention for safety monitoring. Until Enterprise Frontier Safeguards is available, eligible customers can use Fable 5.2 with zero data retention. Visit the Amazon Bedrock abuse detection page to learn more about details regarding data retention for these models.

To learn more, see the Amazon Bedrock documentation, and regional availability.

items.title: Amazon Bedrock now offers Claude Mythos 5.2 to Eligible Customers in AWS GovCloud (US)
items.summary:
Amazon Bedrock, the platform for building generative AI applications and agents at production scale, now offers Claude Mythos 5.2 to eligible customers in AWS GovCloud (US). Claude Mythos 5.2 is Anthropic's most advanced AI model to date for use cases across cybersecurity, software coding, and complex reasoning tasks. The model can identify sophisticated security vulnerabilities in software and demonstrate exploitability. It can also comprehend large codebases and deliver actionable findings with less manual guidance than previous AI models. This enables security teams to accelerate defensive cybersecurity work, find and fix security vulnerabilities in the world's most critical software, and address them before threats emerge. Claude Mythos 5.2 is the first of Anthropic's AI models with powerful cybersecurity capabilities to be available in AWS GovCloud (US).

Claude Mythos 5.2 is available to eligible customers in AWS GovCloud (US) Regions through Amazon Bedrock. Access is limited to allow-listed organizations; to get started, visit Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program.

items.title: Amazon Connect Customer launches evaluation form templates
items.summary:
Amazon Connect Customer now provides evaluation form templates so managers don't have to build forms from scratch, reducing the time to deploy automated evaluations of human and AI agent performance. These templates cover typical customer interaction scenarios: customer service, inbound sales, and self-service. Each template assesses human and AI agent behaviors. For example, the customer service template includes questions such as "Did the agent show empathy toward the customer's issue?" Templates also include questions that assess business outcomes such as customer satisfaction and attrition risk, so managers can see how agent behaviors relate to outcomes. Managers can use the templates as-is or customize them before deploying.

This feature is available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), and Asia Pacific (Tokyo). To learn more, visit our documentation and our webpage. For Amazon Connect Customer pricing, visit our pricing page.

items.title: Amazon MWAA now supports DuckDB operators
items.summary:
Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (Amazon MWAA) now supports DuckDB operators. DuckDB is an embedded analytical database that lets customers perform data quality checks, summaries, and transformations on data from sources DuckDB supports, including Amazon S3.

Native support is available for DuckDB on Amazon MWAA Provisioned environments running Apache Airflow 3.3.1. DuckDB comes preinstalled and preconfigured for AWS connections in the latest MWAA Airflow 3.3.1 update. After updating their MWAA environment to Airflow 3.3.1 and adding execution role access to their data stores, customers can start writing tasks with DuckDBExecuteQueryOperator with no additional setup.

This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon MWAA is available. For more information, see the AWS Region table.

To learn more, see Using DuckDB with Amazon MWAA in the Amazon MWAA User Guide.

items.title: Introducing an open-source UI for graph analytics over data lakes with Amazon Neptune Analytics
items.summary:
Today, AWS is introducing an open-source solution with a local web UI that helps customers turn data lake records into graphs for analysis with Amazon Neptune Analytics. By projecting selected records and relationships, customers can investigate connections across tables and run graph algorithms without building their own ETL pipelines.

For example, a customer could project accounts and transactions into a graph to explore how accounts are connected or identify communities that may warrant investigation. Doing this today often means writing queries to prepare node and relationship data, creating a Neptune Analytics graph, and managing the import. Customers may also need to build a selective projection so they do not load an entire dataset for a narrower question.

The new UI brings those steps into single workflow. To run graph analytics over iceberg tables, customers select an Athena catalog and database, define a property graph using SQL/PGQ, and preview rows before import. The solution runs the projection queries through Athena, stages the selected data in Amazon S3, and imports it into Neptune Analytics. The UI helps customers manage the resulting graph. They can open the loaded graph in Graph Explorer to query and visualize relationships. [1]

The UI runs locally and it is available in all regions where Amazon Neptune Analytics is available. To get started, see the setup instructions.

items.title: Amazon DocumentDB Serverless now provides up to 35% higher throughput
items.summary:
Amazon DocumentDB Serverless now provides up to 35% higher throughput with the launch of platform version 4. Platform versions represent improvements in performance, scaling capabilities, or features, and are automatically managed at the cluster level.

All new serverless clusters launch on the latest platform version available in your AWS Region. You can upgrade existing clusters on platform version 3 to platform version 4 by applying the serverless-platform-version-update pending maintenance action. This gives you control over when to apply the update, either immediately or during your next scheduled maintenance window. After you upgrade to a newer platform version, you can't downgrade to a previous version.

You can view the platform version of a cluster in the AWS Management Console or through the ServerlessV2PlatformVersion field of the DescribeDBClusters API. For more information, see Amazon DocumentDB serverless scaling capacity and Checking and upgrading the platform version of a serverless cluster.

items.title: Amazon Athena introduces system tables for observability, auditing, and usage analytics
items.summary:
Amazon Athena now offers system tables which automatically capture your usage data and make it available for observability, usage analysis, and audit use cases. When you enable system tables, usage data is available within minutes of query completion across your workgroups and stored as service-managed, read-only Iceberg tables on Amazon S3 Tables with configurable retention. You can query it directly with Athena, while AWS manages the tables for you, including schema definition, partitioning, compaction, and snapshot maintenance, removing all operational burden.

Athena provides usage data through APIs like GetQueryExecution, CloudWatch metrics, and CloudTrail logs. With this launch, usage data is also available as iceberg tables that you can search, filter, aggregate, and join directly without building or maintaining custom pipelines. Platform teams can query the query_executions table to build cost allocation dashboards that show data scanned by workgroup, by user, or by table using simple SQL statements, and without custom ETL. Additionally, the AWS Agent Toolkit provides skills for querying system tables to surface usage patterns and optimization recommendations. Because the data is stored in the open Apache Iceberg format, you can also query it with DuckDB, Amazon Redshift, Amazon EMR or any other Iceberg-compatible engine.

Athena system tables are available in all AWS Regions where Athena and Amazon S3 Tables are available. To get started, enable system tables from the Athena console or API. To learn more, visit the Amazon Athena documentation or the  blog.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 is now available on AWS
items.summary:
Claude Fable 5.2 is now available on AWS and brings Anthropic's most capable generally available model for technical work to all customers. Fable 5.2 sets a new standard on the hardest projects in coding, math, and science, and Anthropic recommends it for fields like software engineering, scientific research, and finance, where judgment, iteration, and accuracy are critical. Claude Mythos 5.2, the same underlying model as Claude Fable 5.2 with its full cyber and bio capabilities retained for cybersecurity and biology research, is available through Anthropic’s verification programs.

Claude Fable 5.2 can work for hours and up to days unattended, driving autonomous work and taking on bigger, more challenging projects. It takes on large, loosely defined engineering problems across multiple repositories and monorepos, tests its own work as it goes, and is more willing to question inherited conclusions, so it finds root causes previous Claude models miss. In Anthropic’s testing, it coordinated hundreds of subagents as a lead agent and flagged results that don't reproduce. Beyond coding, it develops new analytical methods for scientific research and brings frontier reasoning to quantitative finance.

Anthropic has designated Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 as covered models, which require data retention for safety monitoring. Until Enterprise Frontier Safeguards is available, eligible customers can use Fable 5.2 with zero data retention. Visit the Amazon Bedrock abuse detection page to learn more about details regarding data retention for these models.

Customers have two ways to access Claude Fable 5.2: Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS. To learn more, see the Amazon Bedrock documentation, regional availability, and Claude Platform on AWS documentation.

items.title: AWS Analytics services now support Workday Data Cloud integration
items.summary:
Today, AWS announces a new bi-directional, zero-copy integration between AWS Analytics services and Workday Data Cloud. Instead of building and maintaining ETL pipelines to replicate data between systems, joint customers can now query across their AWS and Workday datasets in place, without moving or copying data, while retaining existing security controls in both environments.

From AWS, you can use Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon EMR, AWS Glue, Amazon Redshift, and Amazon Athena to query Workday data through Workday Live Data Query or federate to Apache Iceberg tables in Workday Data Cloud through catalog federation. Configure a connection in SageMaker Unified Studio, AWS Glue, or AWS Lake Formation consoles and begin querying immediately. Access is governed by AWS and Workday permissions.

From Workday, you can register your AWS Glue Data Catalog Iceberg REST endpoint as an external catalog in Workday Analytics and query your AWS Iceberg tables directly. Common use cases include joining workforce data with business data for talent analytics, workforce planning, and machine learning.

This integration is available in all AWS commercial regions where AWS Glue is available. To learn more, see the AWS Glue User Guide, the Workday Data Cloud integration with AWS on Workday Data Cloud, and the AWS Big Data Blog post.

items.title: Amazon S3 Access Points for Amazon FSx are now available in additional AWS Regions
items.summary:
You can now attach Amazon S3 Access Points to your Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file systems in 4 additional AWS Regions, and to your Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file systems in 20 additional AWS Regions. With this capability, your file data in Amazon FSx is accessible for use with the broad range of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and analytics services and applications that work with S3, while your data continues to reside on your FSx file system.

An S3 Access Point for Amazon FSx is an S3 endpoint that gives S3-based applications and services access to the data on your FSx file system through the Amazon S3 API, without copying or moving that data. For example, you can connect generative AI applications and agents to your file data with Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases so they deliver relevant, contextual responses. Users can query the same data in place with Amazon Athena or transform it with AWS Glue, and you can share files with partners over SFTP, FTPS, and FTP using AWS Transfer Family. You can also access your files from serverless compute such as Amazon ECS and AWS Fargate, or from your own S3-based applications.

Amazon S3 Access Points for FSx for ONTAP and FSx for OpenZFS are now available in additional AWS Regions across North America, South America, Europe, Asia Pacific, and Africa. For the full list of AWS Regions supported for each file system, see the FSx for ONTAP and FSx for OpenZFS user guides. Get started by creating and attaching S3 Access Points using the Amazon FSx console, the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI), or the AWS Software Development Kit (AWS SDK). To learn more, visit the Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP and Amazon FSx for OpenZFS product pages, the Amazon S3 Access Points page, and the FSx for ONTAP and OpenZFS user guides.

items.title: Introducing AWS Nitro Sandboxes on Amazon EKS, ECS and EC2 for hardware isolated pods, tasks and VMs
items.summary:
AWS Nitro Sandboxes are now available as lightweight VMs managed by the Nitro Hypervisor. You can use Nitro Sandboxes for an Amazon EKS pod, or Amazon ECS task, or lightweight Virtual Machines (VMs), including AI agents running inside them, in their own hardware-isolated virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro System. Each workload gets the isolation boundary of a Nitro isolated virtual machine. This allows you to safely run untrusted, multi-tenant, or regulated workloads within the resources of a single instance.

Nitro Sandboxes run on your EC2 instances with near-native EC2 performance and inherits Nitro-hypervisor isolation. You can also validate your workloads through cryptographic attestation, so that secrets are released only to Nitro Sandboxes that have proven their integrity. With Nitro Sandboxes, you can safely execute LLM-generated code in an isolated environment of its own all while improving utilization and lowering compute costs by securely sharing a single EC2 instance across multiple agentic workloads. You can easily enable EKS pods or ECS tasks to run on Nitro Sandboxes and each pod or task gets its own isolated environment. Enabling Nitro Sandboxes in EKS or ECS is a one-line change and each pod or task gets its own VM, with your workloads remaining fully native (Pod Identity, VPC CNI, EBS/EFS/S3 storage, and CloudWatch all work out of the box). If you want full control, run Nitro Sandboxes directly on EC2 with your own AMI, orchestration, and with virtual machine monitors (VMMs). Amazon Linux and Firecracker are natively supported, and patches for other options are available today.

AWS Nitro Sandboxes are available today on most Nitro-based EC2 instances, in all commercial regions worldwide, at no additional charge.

To learn more and get started, see the EKS User Guide or ECS User Guide. For implementation details or to fully customize your Nitro Sandbox usage, see the Nitro Sandboxes documentation in the EC2 user guide.

items.title: Amazon Route 53 Profiles now supports multiple Profiles per VPC
items.summary:
Amazon Route 53 Profiles now lets you associate more than one Profile with a VPC. Previously, a VPC could have only one Profile, so teams that managed Route 53 configurations separately (for example, security teams managing DNS Firewall rule groups while cloud infrastructure and network admin teams manage private hosted zones and Resolver forwarding rules) all had to share a single Profile and associate their private hosted zones, Resolver rules, and DNS Firewall rule groups with it.

With this launch, you can now associate multiple Profiles with the same VPC and set a priority for every Profile. Route 53 evaluates a VPC's Profiles in priority order, starting with the lowest number, so you can keep shared Route 53 configurations in one Profile and team-specific configurations in another without merging them, while assigning them the right priority. Combined with the granular IAM permissions launched in March 2026, multiple Profiles per VPC improves security posture by letting each team own and manage its own Profile with least-privilege permissions.

This capability is available in all AWS Regions where Route 53 Profiles is available.

Each Profile-VPC association is billed at standard Route 53 Profiles pricing. For details, see Amazon Route 53 pricing. To learn more, see Route 53 Profiles in the Amazon Route 53 Developer Guide.

items.title: Amazon EKS Auto Mode and Karpenter now support Dynamic Resource Allocation
items.summary:
Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) now supports Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) for NVIDIA GPUs and Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) network devices when using Amazon EKS Auto Mode and Karpenter. You can now define the device attributes your Kubernetes workloads need with DRA, share GPU devices across Pods, and allocate topology-aligned GPU and EFA devices while Amazon EKS Auto Mode and Karpenter dynamically scale Amazon EC2 instances based on workload demand.

With DRA, you define ResourceClaim or ResourceClaimTemplate objects that describe what GPU or EFA devices can be allocated to workloads, by model, architecture, or other attributes. When running distributed training or inference, you can define PCIe-aligned GPU and EFA devices for optimal performance. Workloads then request those DRA objects in their configuration, and Karpenter automatically launches the lowest-cost instances that match. When using Amazon EKS Auto Mode, the NVIDIA DRA driver and EFA DRA driver (DRANET) are built-in, and you simply define your DRA objects and use them in your workloads. Amazon EKS Auto Mode automatically prevents workloads using DRA and workloads using device plugins for the same device type from running on the same nodes to mitigate the risk of silent device oversubscription during migrations.

DRA support for Amazon EKS Auto Mode and Karpenter is available in all AWS Regions, except the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions and the China Regions. DRA support is available for all Kubernetes versions in Karpenter, and for Kubernetes versions 1.36 and newer in Amazon EKS Auto Mode. To learn more, see the DRA documentation in the Amazon EKS User Guide and Karpenter documentation.

items.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro (Highspeed) now available on Amazon Bedrock
items.summary:
Today, Kimi K3.1 Pro from Moonshot AI is available on Amazon Bedrock, expanding our open weight model portfolio with the security and governance that customers rely on. Customers using Amazon Bedrock can now run agentic use cases such as coding and document processing on Kimi K3.1 Pro (Highspeed), which delivers high output tokens per second (OTPS) for faster, more responsive results.

According to Moonshot AI, Kimi K3.1 Pro is an open-weight, natively multimodal agentic model with a 1-million-token context window, and its most capable 3-trillion-parameter-class model to date. Moonshot AI reports improvements in coding, 3D creation, financial research, and other agentic work. On Amazon Bedrock, it runs within the same security boundary as proprietary models and supports explicit prompt caching to reduce latency and input costs.

Kimi K3.1 Pro is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Bedrock is available through cross-Region inference. To get started, visit the Amazon Bedrock console. To learn more, see the Amazon Bedrock documentation.

items.title: Agent Registry is now generally available in AWS GovCloud (US-West) Region
items.summary:
AWS Agent Registry, available through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, is now available in the AWS GovCloud (US-West) Region.

AWS Agent Registry is a fully managed discovery service that gives your organization a central catalog for organizing, curating, and discovering resources. You can publish MCP servers, tools, agents, agent skills, and custom resources to a searchable registry, and control what becomes discoverable through an approval workflow. People and AI agents can then find the right tools and agents through hybrid search, catalog browsing, and a native MCP endpoint.

With Agent Registry in AWS GovCloud (US-West), public sector organizations and their partners get a single governed inventory of the agents and tools in their environment. Approval workflows and AWS CloudTrail audit logs support their compliance and oversight requirements.

To get started, see the AWS Agent Registry documentation.

items.title: Amazon MWAA Serverless supports Apache Airflow connections and variables
items.summary:
Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (Amazon MWAA) Serverless now supports Apache Airflow connections and variables, so your workflows can reach databases, APIs, and other external systems. You can manage credentials and configuration outside your workflow code.

You store sensitive connections and variables in the secrets backend of your choice, such as AWS Secrets Manager, AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, or your own custom backend, configure it on your workflow, and grant your workflow execution role access. Tasks retrieve them at run time through standard Apache Airflow methods. You can define non-secret values as environment variables on the workflow.

This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon MWAA Serverless is available. For more information, see Amazon MWAA Serverless Regions.

To learn more, see Managing connections and variables and Using environment variables in Amazon MWAA Serverless workflows in the Amazon MWAA Serverless User Guide.

items.title: Amazon MWAA Serverless now supports custom and provider package operators
items.summary:
Amazon MWAA Serverless now supports operators from Apache Airflow provider packages, such as HTTP, Snowflake, or dbt, and custom operators that you write. This gives data engineers the flexibility to integrate with more systems and build specialized workflow tasks without provisioning infrastructure.

To get started, add the provider package or your own operator to a code package, upload it to Amazon S3, and reference the operator in your workflow definition when you create or update a workflow.

This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon MWAA Serverless is available. For a list of supported Regions, see Amazon MWAA Serverless Regions. To learn more, see Running custom code with Python, Bash, and custom operators in the Amazon MWAA Serverless User Guide.

items.title: Amazon MSK Replicator is now available in AWS GovCloud (US-East, US-West) Regions
items.summary:
You can now use Amazon MSK Replicator in the AWS GovCloud (US-East, US-West) Regions to replicate streaming data across Amazon MSK clusters and from external Apache Kafka clusters including on-premises, self-managed on AWS, or other cloud providers to Amazon MSK Provisioned clusters.

MSK Replicator is a feature of Amazon MSK that automates data replication between Kafka clusters, eliminating the need to manage custom replication infrastructure or configure open-source tools. With MSK Replicator, you can easily build regionally resilient streaming applications for increased availability and business continuity. MSK Replicator provides automatic asynchronous replication across Kafka clusters, eliminating the need to write custom code, manage infrastructure, or setup cross-region networking. MSK Replicator automatically scales the underlying resources so that you can replicate data on-demand without having to monitor or scale capacity. MSK Replicator also replicates the necessary Kafka metadata including topic configurations, Access Control Lists (ACLs), and consumer group offsets. If an unexpected event occurs in a region, you can failover to the other AWS Region and seamlessly resume processing.

You can get started with MSK Replicator from the Amazon MSK console or the Amazon CLI. To learn more, visit the MSK Replicator documentation, product page, and pricing page.

items.title: Amazon Redshift expands SUPER data type to store strings up to 16 million bytes
items.summary:
Amazon Redshift now supports individual strings up to 16 million bytes within SUPER data types. Once you opt in through a database parameter, this enhancement applies when ingesting structured or semi-structured data from JSON, PARQUET, TEXT, and CSV source files, and when transforming data through extract load and transform (ELT) processes. Previously, individual strings within SUPER data types were limited to 65,535 bytes.

Storing large individual strings in the SUPER data type helps avoid complex pre-loading transformations needed to store the source data in Amazon Redshift. You can now directly ingest large individual strings greater than 65,535 bytes without extra processing (for example, lengthy documents like terms and conditions and contracts), making them queryable using SQL. Once the data is in Amazon Redshift, you can use the flexibility of PartiQL language to explore and navigate through the data or use string functions to transform the data. Functions such as JSON_PARSE, CONCAT, and LISTAGG can now take input strings and return output strings up to 16 million bytes in length.

This enhancement is available in all AWS Regions, including the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, where Amazon Redshift is available. See the AWS Region Table for more details. To learn more, please visit our documentation or blog.

items.title: AWS launches support for amortization of EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML
items.summary:
AWS Data Exports for Cost and Usage Report (CUR) 2.0 and AWS Cost Explorer now amortize the upfront fee for Amazon EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML across the duration of each reservation. You can see the amortized cost of each instance launched into a Capacity Block and the amortized cost of unused capacity, so you can attribute your upfront fee to the workloads that used it and identify capacity that went unused.

Previously, a Capacity Block's upfront fee appeared as a single charge on the purchase date, making it difficult to see how that cost was spread across usage over the reservation. Now the amortized cost appears alongside your instance usage, so you can allocate GPU costs to the teams, projects, and applications that ran on the reserved capacity. You can also see what share of your reservation went unused and plan future Capacity Block purchases. In CUR 2.0, the amortized costs appear in the reservation_amortized_upfront_fee_for_billing_period, reservation_effective_cost columns, and reservation_net_effective_cost shows the amortized cost after discounts. In Cost Explorer, select the amortized cost view to see Capacity Block costs allocated for the reservation.

 Amortization for Capacity Blocks is available at no additional charge in all AWS Regions except the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions and the China Regions. To learn more, see the CUR 2.0 data dictionary and exploring your data using Cost Explorer.

items.title: Capacity Reservation Resource Groups now support Amazon EC2 Capacity Blocks and interruptible Capacity Reservations in AWS GovCloud (US) Regions
items.summary:
Starting today, you can add Amazon EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML and interruptible Capacity Reservations to Capacity Reservation Resource Groups in AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. Amazon EC2 offers different reservation offerings such as On-Demand Capacity Reservations (ODCRs), interruptible Capacity Reservations, and Capacity Blocks for ML. Previously, a Capacity Reservation Resource Group could only include ODCRs. Now you can add any type of Capacity Reservation to a Capacity Reservation Resource Group, making it easier to launch EC2 instances across your entire portfolio of reserved capacity.

To use this feature, create a Capacity Reservation Resource Group, add any Capacity Reservation to it, and then target the group in your launch request. When using EC2 Fleet and EC2 Auto Scaling groups, you can also specify your prioritization preferences across reservation types, and configure automatic fall back to EC2 On-Demand capacity when there is no capacity remaining across your reservations.

There are no additional charges for using this feature. With the addition of AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, this feature is now available in all AWS Regions where Capacity Blocks for ML and interruptible ODCRs are supported, excluding China Regions. To get started, see Capacity Reservation Resource Groups and the Capacity Reservations user guide.

items.title: Amazon Simple Email Service is now available in six new AWS Regions
items.summary:
Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES)  is now available in the Asia Pacific (New Zealand, Melbourne, Taipei, Thailand), Mexico (Central), EU (Spain). Customers can now use these new Regions to leverage Amazon SES to send emails and, if needed, to help manage data requirements.

Amazon SES is a scalable, cost-effective, and flexible cloud-based email service that allows digital marketers and application developers to send marketing, notification, and transactional emails from within any application. To learn more about Amazon SES, visit this page .

With this launch, Amazon SES is available in 35 AWS Regions globally: US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (N. California, Oregon), AWS GovCloud (US-West, US-East), Asia Pacific (Osaka, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Sydney, Singapore, Seoul, Tokyo, Jakarta, Malaysia, New Zealand, Melbourne, Taipei, Thailand), Canada (Central, Calgary), EU (Ireland, Frankfurt, London, Paris, Stockholm, Milan, Zurich,Spain), Middle East (Bahrain, UAE), Israel (Tel Aviv), South America (Sao Paulo), Mexico (Central) and Africa (Cape Town).

For a complete list of all of the regional endpoints for Amazon SES, see  AWS Service Endpoints  in the AWS General Reference.

items.title: AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports catalog-vended credentials with Apache Iceberg REST catalog federation
items.summary:
AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports external catalog's vended credentials in Apache Iceberg REST catalog federation. You can now read external Iceberg tables from Amazon Athena, Amazon EMR, Amazon Redshift, and AWS Glue using coarse-grained table grants in your external Iceberg catalog.

Glue Data Catalog already federates to external Iceberg REST catalogs through an AWS IAM role that you configure with access to your Amazon S3 buckets. This enhancement in Glue Data Catalog provides another way to connect to an external Iceberg catalog and read only the tables that the external catalog authorizes. It uses temporary security credentials that are scoped to the Amazon S3 storage prefix and vended by your external Iceberg catalog. AWS Lake Formation manages access control when you query an external table using any AWS analytics engine, letting you restrict access further down to specific rows and columns and share external Iceberg tables across AWS accounts.

This feature is available through the AWS Lake Formation Management Console, AWS CLI, and the AWS Glue and Lake Formation SDKs. This feature is available in all commercial AWS Regions where Glue and Lake Formation are supported. To learn more, visit the documentation.

items.title: AWS Elemental MediaConvert adds a native integration with AWS Elemental Inference Smart Subtitles
items.summary:
​​AWS Elemental MediaConvert now integrates Smart Subtitles, an AI-powered subtitling solution built on AWS Elemental Inference and the latest speech recognition models. This feature brings automated subtitle generation directly into your video-on-demand (VOD) transcoding and packaging workflows, eliminating the need for separate external captioning pipelines. Customers can now manage both transcoding and subtitle creation within a single, unified workflow.

​Smart subtitles automatically transcribe your audio into subtitles with native support for six languages including English, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, and Spanish. With MediaConvert, you can package the outputs to text-based side-car formats and burn-in for all your streaming or distribution needs. To enhance transcription quality, you can now define custom dictionaries in Elemental Inference to guide the model on proper nouns, brand names, technical terminology, and more. Smart subtitles complement existing add-on features such as Smart Cropping for end-to-end media pipelines, intelligent framing and accessible subtitle delivery in distribution-ready formats like HLS and DASH.​

​​Smart subtitles is available in all AWS regions where Elemental Inference is available including US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Europe (Ireland), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), and Asia Pacific (Sydney).​

To learn more, visit Smart subtitles with MediaConvert, AWS Elemental MediaConvert  and AWS Elemental Inference smart subtitles.

items.title: AWS Security Hub now provides an SBOM inventory for your compute resources
items.summary:
Today, AWS announces that AWS Security Hub now provides a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) inventory, giving central security teams a continuously updated, organization-wide view of the software packages and applications installed on their compute resources.

Security Hub builds the inventory from the SBOMs that Amazon Inspector generates for Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon ECR container images, and AWS Lambda functions, with no additional configuration. The SBOM page lists each package with its version, type, and the number of resources where it is installed. You can filter and group the list by package attributes, account, and region. On the resource detail page, the Installed software tab lists every package on that resource, so you can judge its function and criticality while triaging any finding. You can also query the inventory through the Security Hub API.

The SBOM inventory is included with Security Hub Essentials at no additional cost. It requires no new enablement and populates automatically where Amazon Inspector is enabled. It is available in all AWS Regions where Security Hub is available. To learn more, see the AWS Security Hub User Guide and the AWS Security Hub product page.

items.title: AWS Interconnect - last mile announces new metro in Northern Virginia, USA
items.summary:
Today, AWS announced a new AWS Interconnect - last mile metro in Northern Virginia, USA. Northern Virginia joins New York as the second metro where you can connect your data center, branch office, or colocation facility to AWS. 

AWS Interconnect - last mile gives you managed, private, resilient connections to AWS, so you don't have to order cross-connects or configure routers. Every connection is provisioned by default across two physically diverse locations with four redundant links, providing maximum resilience out of the box and backed by a 99.99% availability SLA up to the Direct Connect port. Traffic between AWS and partner edge devices is encrypted with MACsec by default.

Lumen customers anywhere in the continental United States can order generally available connections through the Northern Virginia metro to reach all public AWS Regions (except those in China) and AWS Local Zones. AWS Interconnect - last mile is also available in preview through Megaport and Equinix in the Northern Virginia metro. You can create connections using the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, or AWS Interconnect API. For pricing, see AWS Interconnect - last mile pricing.

items.title: Announcing Web Answer on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
items.summary:
Today, we are announcing the general availability of Web Answer on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Web Answer is a managed tool that returns a synthesized, grounded, cited answer to a natural-language question in a single call, so agent builders can attach it to an agent and get back a finished answer grounded in current web sources, without building and maintaining their own search, retrieve, synthesis, and citation pipeline. 

Web Answer builds on Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, which launched in June, extending it from "find the web content" to "return the finished answer," a capability customers have been asking for. With Web Answer, your agent sends a question and receives a synthesized cited answer in one tool call. Web Answer works like an agent; it plans its own searches, runs several in parallel, and decides when it has gathered enough evidence to answer. You stay in control of the boundaries, with domain include, deny lists and publish-date filters that scope where it looks. It attaches as a target on an AgentCore Gateway and is called over MCP, authenticated with IAM, with zero data egress. 

Web Answer is available in the US East (N. Virginia) Region, with per-tool call pricing. 

To learn more about Web Answer on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, see Web Answer’s documentation page and Web Answer’s website. For Region availability, see the AWS Region table.

items.title: AWS Network Load Balancer is now available in the AWS Phoenix Local Zone
items.summary:
AWS Network Load Balancer is now available in the Phoenix Local Zone (us-west-2-phx-2a). AWS Local Zones is a type of AWS infrastructure deployment that places AWS compute, storage, database, and other select services closer to large population, industry, and IT centers where no AWS Region exists today.

With this launch, you can create an AWS Network Load Balancer directly in the Phoenix Local Zone. Previously, if your targets ran in the Phoenix Local Zone, you had to place the load balancer in an Availability Zone in the parent Region, so connections and their traffic had to travel to the parent Region and back. This added latency and routed traffic outside the zone where your application runs. Now, connection routing stays local to your targets, delivering lower and more consistent latency to end users in the Phoenix metro area and keeping traffic within the Local Zone. This is especially valuable for latency-sensitive workloads such as real-time gaming, media streaming, and live financial applications serving users in the region.

To learn more about Network Load Balancer, visit the documentation. For more information on AWS Local Zones, visit the AWS Local Zones website. The Locations webpage lists the available and announced Local Zones. You can enable AWS Local Zones from the Local Zones tab in the AWS Global View console, or the ModifyAvailabilityZoneGroup API.

items.title: Amazon DynamoDB now supports bulk put items
items.summary:
Today, AWS announces the general availability of bulk put items for Amazon DynamoDB, a fully managed feature that writes data from Amazon S3 into your existing DynamoDB tables. Many DynamoDB applications use data that other systems produce and store in Amazon S3. Writing this data into existing DynamoDB tables has typically meant building custom pipelines and managing table capacity. With bulk put items, developers and data engineers can write this data without impacting existing workloads or building a custom ingestion pipeline, in a cost-efficient way.

You point bulk put items at the S3 location of your input files, and DynamoDB handles the rest. Each item supports its own condition expression, so you can enforce insert-only or version-guarded writes. The Standard tier fits most workloads, and the Accelerated tier is for more time-sensitive workloads. Common use cases include daily refreshes, large catalog enrichments, backfills, and migrations.

Bulk put items with Standard tier is available in all commercial AWS Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, to see the list where the Accelerated tier is available see the regional availability. To learn more, visit the Introducing bulk put items for Amazon DynamoDB blog and the Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide.

items.title: 製造業 7 社が率直に語った AI エージェント全社基盤の実践と課題：生成 AI 基盤・活用推進 ラウンドテーブル 2026年10月 開催報告

items.title: AIが進め、人が決める ― AI駆動開発の本当のボトルネックはどこにあったか
items.summary: こんにちは。AWS ソリューションアーキテクトの崔 祐碩（Woosuk Choi）です。AI 開発を進めている多くのお客様から「開発を加速したい」というご相談をいただいています。お客様と議論を重ねるたびに、本当のボトルネックは開発そのものではなく、意思決定をめぐるプロセスと組織ではないか、と感じることが増えてきました。本ブログでは、2026年7月29日に MBK Wellness 株式会社と実施した AI-DLC ワークショップを題材に、私たちがこの仮説をどう確かめ、どんな答えが返ってきたのかをご紹介します。

items.title: AWS Nitro Sandboxes: Amazon EKS で実現するハードウェア強制型ワークロード分離
items.summary: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) 向けに AWS Nitro Sandboxes の提供を開始しました。サンドボックス化されたポッドは AWS Nitro System を基盤とする専用の軽量 VM で実行されるため、ポッドごとにハードウェアベースのセキュリティ境界を設けられます。EKS Auto Mode ではポッド仕様を 1 行変更するだけで有効にでき、分離モードと機密モードを選べます。AI エージェント、マルチテナント SaaS、規制対象のワークロードを安全かつ効率的に実行する方法を、AI コーディングエージェントの実行例とともに紹介します。

items.title: AMS Trusted Remediator でコスト最適化とセキュリティ修復を自動化する
items.summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) を活用している組織は、セキュリティとコスト最適化に関する推奨事項を毎月数千件も受け取ります。しかし、優先順位の問題やリソースの制約からその多くは実施されないままとなっています。AWS Managed Services (AMS) の Trusted Remediator はこの課題を解決するため、複数の AWS アカウントにわたる修復を自動化し、手作業による修復にかかる時間と手間を大幅に減らします。あらかじめ用意された修復ライブラリは、116 件の推奨事項に対応しており、新しい機能が加わるたびに増え続けています。これらの自動化は、セキュリティ、コスト最適化、運用上の優秀性の各分野にわたります。企業はセキュリティホールを効率よくふさぎ、コストを最適化し、コンプライアンスを維持しながら AWS のベストプラクティスの変化にも柔軟に対応できます。

items.title: AWS 上の Microsoft ワークロード: re:Invent 2026 完全ガイド
items.summary: AWS re:Invent 2026 では、AWS 上で Microsoft ワークロードを実行しているお客様向けに充実したセッションを用意しています。AWS Transform と Kiro によるエージェンティック AI での .NET と SQL Server のモダナイゼーション、ライセンスコストの削減、VMware からの移行、レジリエンスの高い運用まで、ぜひ参加していただきたいセッションを紹介します。

items.title: 【開催報告】ランサムウェアに備える「防御」「復旧」「説明責任」— AI エージェント時代に見直す対策と次の一歩
items.summary: 2026 年 10 月 26 日に開催したセキュリティセミナーの開催報告です。「防御・検知」「説明責任」「復旧」の 3 つの軸で、AWS とパートナー 5 社のセッション内容と、軸ごとにまず着手したい対策をまとめました。

items.title: インフラストラクチャの移行: AWS re:Invent 2026 完全ガイド
items.summary: AWS re:Invent 2026 (11 月 30 日〜12 月 4 日、ラスベガス) では、AWS Transform のエージェント型 AI が移行ライフサイクル全体をどのように自動化するかを紹介するセッションが多数用意されています。本記事では、移行戦略とお客様事例、ビジネスケースの構築、AWS Transform と Amazon EVS のハンズオンセッション、AWS Outposts への移行、そして移行後のモダナイゼーションまで、インフラ移行に関するセッションを厳選して紹介します。

items.title: Amazon Bedrock を活用したアプリケーションの設計に信頼と安全性を組み込む
items.summary: Amazon Bedrock を活用した生成 AI アプリケーションでは、設計段階から安全性を組み込むことが重要です。本記事では、責任ある AI の主要な側面と、設計と開発、デプロイ、運用の各フェーズで安全性を確保するための考え方を解説します。さらに、Amazon CloudWatch による監視や Amazon Bedrock Guardrails による保護措置のカスタマイズなど、不正使用を防止する方法を紹介します。AWS Trust & Safety チームから不正使用の報告を受けた際の対応プロセスも説明します。

items.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Policy がエージェンティックワークフローの保護に Cedar を採用した理由
items.summary: AI エージェントの中核にある大規模言語モデル (LLM) は非決定論的で、ハルシネーションやプロンプトインジェクションのリスクがあります。本記事では、LLM を信頼できないアクターとして扱う考え方を説明します。そのうえで、Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway でツール呼び出しを認可制御する AgentCore Policy が Cedar を採用した理由を解説します。可読性、決定論的な動作、自動推論による分析可能性を活かして、ニューロシンボリック AI でポリシーを作成し、Cedar Analysis で論理エラーや競合を検出する仕組みも紹介します。
